classification.difficultyReason: Direct application of the explicitly taught input absolute-value transformation to recognise a graph from four options; no additional insight or linked procedure is essential.

content.prompt: The graph of $f(x)=(x-1)^2$ is shown as a dotted line. Which graph represents $y=(|x|-1)^2$?

spec.description: Four-option row, first panel. Arrowed axes with integer ticks from −3 to 3, excluding zero; no grid. Solid symmetric double-valley graph and dashed base parabola. The origin O label is omitted under the graph contract.
spec.mathematics: Dashed base y=(x-1)^2. Solid option y=(|x|-1)^2, with minima at (−1,0) and (1,0) and a sharp central maximum at (0,1). Curves continue beyond the displayed window.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent multiple-choice option; contains no answer-selection annotation.

spec.description: Second panel in the four-option row. Matching arrowed axes and integer ticks, no grid. Solid upward parabola covers the coincident dashed base.
spec.mathematics: Both the dashed base and solid option are y=(x-1)^2, with vertex (1,0) and y-intercept (0,1). Curves continue beyond the displayed window.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent multiple-choice option; contains no answer-selection annotation.

spec.description: Third panel in the four-option row. Matching arrowed axes and integer ticks, no grid. Solid symmetric upward branches meet at a sharp minimum at (0,1); the dashed base has vertex (1,0).
spec.mathematics: Dashed base y=(x-1)^2. Solid option y=(|x|+1)^2. Its left branch coincides with the base for x≤0. Curves continue beyond the displayed window.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent multiple-choice option; contains no answer-selection annotation.

spec.description: Fourth panel in the four-option row. Matching arrowed axes and integer ticks, no grid. Solid upward parabola has vertex (−1,0); dashed base has vertex (1,0).
spec.mathematics: Dashed base y=(x-1)^2. Solid option y=(x+1)^2. Both pass through (0,1) and continue beyond the displayed window.
spec.answerVisibility: Permanent multiple-choice option; contains no answer-selection annotation.

answer.worked:
Keep the portion of $y=(x-1)^2$ for $x\geq0$ and reflect it across the $y$-axis, replacing the original left-hand portion. The resulting graph is symmetric about the $y$-axis, with minima at $(-1,0)$ and $(1,0)$ and a sharp central maximum at $(0,1)$.

Correct answer: A.
